guard: An existing space keeps its posts older than 30 days, on the limit it had, through a `cotal up` that starts its broker, and a new space starts with no age limit and 1000 per sender. A restore holds the chat stream at the recorded count and no age through every check of the restored state, then sets the age the backup recorded on the target and reads it back, and a backup on the old settings keeps them at the next start. A `cotal setup --start` whose manager identity does not read afterwards reports an unknown outcome with that reason.
command: pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/core build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/cli build && pnpm smoke:chat-history-restore:live
why: The suite drives `tsx bin/cotal.ts`, which loads core and the CLI from their built dist, so each mutation
rebuilds both and `afterRestore` rebuilds them from the restored source. The aged-posts scenario backdates its
posts in the stopped broker's store and then starts it with `cotal up`, so a start that moved the limit to an
age would watch the broker delete them. The recorded-age scenario's posts are older than the recorded age when
the restore checks them, so a restore that set the age first would watch the broker delete them during its
